name: Claude 4.5 Sonnet
description: High-intelligence flagship model balancing deep reasoning, coding capabilities, and execution speed.
strengths: State-of-the-art software engineering and agentic workflows
Long context retention across 1M tokens
Reliable instruction following and tool use
weaknesses: Higher output token price than flash-tier models
Rate limits during peak enterprise demand

name: Claude 4.5 Opus
description: Top-tier reasoning model built for complex open-ended problems, intricate coding, and rigorous analysis.
strengths: Exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks
Nuanced writing style and deep contextual synthesis
Top-tier reliability for critical tasks
weaknesses: Slower generation time than Sonnet or Haiku
Premium pricing per million tokens

name: Claude 4.5 Haiku
description: Ultra-fast and cost-effective compact model for everyday chat, summarization, and lightweight coding.
strengths: Near-instant response latency
Very affordable token pricing
High accuracy for structured tasks and extraction
weaknesses: Less depth on multi-step novel reasoning
Smaller maximum completion length

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
description: Multimodal workhorse with a native 1M+ token context window, strong cross-modal understanding, and deep tool calling.
strengths: Huge 1M token context for whole codebases and video analysis
Strong multimodal reasoning (audio, video, images, pdfs)
Competitive mid-tier pricing
weaknesses: Can be verbose on simple inquiries
Output generation speeds vary under high load

name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
description: Lightweight, high-throughput model built for low-latency tasks and high-volume multimodal pipelines.
strengths: Sub-second latency on most prompts
Extremely economical pricing ($0.30/1M input)
Full 1M token window with multimodal inputs
weaknesses: Prone to surface-level solutions on difficult bugs
Less stylistic control for creative writing

name: GPT-4o
description: Versatile multimodal flagship model designed for fast, natural conversation and everyday knowledge tasks.
strengths: Strong conversational fluency and emotional nuance
Fast response times and broad tool integration
Broad language and vision coverage
weaknesses: Context window limited to 128K compared to 1M peers
Lower software agent benchmark scores than specialized reasoning models

name: GPT-4o mini
description: Compact, affordable OpenAI model suited for high-volume conversational tasks, lightweight processing, and filtering.
strengths: Very affordable input and output rates
Low latency for UI interactions
Consistent structured output generation
weaknesses: Limited capability on complex math and programming
128K context window

name: OpenAI o1
description: Reasoning model trained with reinforcement learning to think through math, science, and coding problems before responding.
strengths: Industry-leading performance on competition math and science
Deep chain-of-thought self-correction
Strong adherence to complex constraints
weaknesses: High latency due to reasoning tokens
Premium pricing ($15 / $60 per 1M tokens)
Not designed for fast conversational back-and-forth

name: OpenAI o3-mini
description: Efficient reasoning model tailored for science, math, and coding with customizable reasoning effort and low API costs.
strengths: High coding performance at a fraction of o1 cost
Adjustable reasoning effort levels (low, medium, high)
Fast generation speeds for a reasoning model
weaknesses: Text-only inputs (no vision support)
Reasoning tokens contribute to billed token count

name: DeepSeek V3
description: Open-weights mixture-of-experts model delivering frontier-level intelligence at disruptive cost efficiency.
strengths: Extremely affordable API pricing ($0.32/$0.89 per 1M)
Frontier-grade knowledge and general intelligence
Permissive open-weights licensing
weaknesses: No native image or audio support
Occasional queue latency during peak global traffic

name: DeepSeek R1
description: Open-weights reasoning model using large-scale reinforcement learning for math, coding, and logical deductions.
strengths: Rivals closed-source reasoning models on math and logic
Open weights and transparent chain-of-thought
Very low API pricing for a reasoning model
weaknesses: Thinking process can be verbose for simple tasks
Limited context window (64K)

name: Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B
description: Specialized coding model with open weights, strong repository-level understanding, and high multi-language accuracy.
strengths: Can be self-hosted on a single GPU
Highly competitive coding performance against much larger models
Very economical cloud hosting
weaknesses: Smaller 32K context window on default deployments
Lower performance on non-code creative writing

name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
description: Flagship open-weights model from Meta offering 405B-class performance at 70B efficiency for broad enterprise use.
strengths: Industry-standard open weights with extensive community support
Ultra-cheap cloud API pricing ($0.10/$0.32 per 1M)
Solid general reasoning and instruction following
weaknesses: Text-only (no native vision modality)
Lags frontier proprietary models on complex agent benchmarks

name: Mistral Large 2
description: European flagship model with exceptional multilingual capabilities, concise reasoning, and strong code generation.
strengths: Excellent multilingual fluency (French, German, Spanish, Italian)
Precise tool and function calling support
High-performance structured output compliance
weaknesses: Moderate API pricing relative to open models
No native image or audio generation
